9307               	;
9308               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
9309               	; 	'
9310               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
9311               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
9312               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
9313               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
9314               	; 	'
9315               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
9316               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
9317               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
9318               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9319               	; 	'
9320               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
9321               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
9322               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
9323               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
9324               	; 	'
9325               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
9326               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
9327               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
9328               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
9329               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for
9330               	; 	' a genuine stall and at five it only fires for one.

9818               	;
9819               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9820               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9821               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9822               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9823               	; 	' runs every pass.
9824               	; 	'
9825               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9826               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9827               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9828               	; 	'
9829               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9830               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9831               	; 	'
9832               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9833               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9834               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9835               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9836               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9837               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9838               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9839               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9840               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9841               	; 	'
9842               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9843               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9844               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9845               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9846               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9847               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9848               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9849               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
9850               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
9851               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
9852               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the
9853               	; 	' flight looking busy.
9854               	; 	'
9855               	; 	' TWO THINGS END THE RUN, AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE ON SCREEN.
9856               	; 	'
9857               	; 	' THE KOP ARRIVING ON THIS FLOOR OUTRANKS IT. This used to override the

9949               	;
9950               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9951               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9952               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9953               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9954               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9955               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9956               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9957               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9958               	; 	'
9959               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9960               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9961               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9962               	; 	'
9963               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9964               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9965               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9966               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9967               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9968               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9969               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9970               	; 	'
9971               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9972               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9973               	; 	'
9974               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9975               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9976               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9977               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9978               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9979               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9980               	; 	'
9981               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9982               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9983               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9984               	; 	' before any of this.
9985               	; 	'
9986               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9987               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9988               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
9989               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
9990               	; 	' journey.
9991               	; 	'
9992               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels

10171               	; 	' hspd is 0 on a third of his frames. On every one of those the legs took
10172               	; 	' another step while the ground did not move, which is precisely what
10173               	; 	' scrubbing your feet looks like. It is the classic foot-slip: the legs
10174               	; 	' and the world running off two different clocks.

10177               	; 	' without covering ground, or cover ground without taking one, at any

10442 E000 0450  20 	b *r0
10443               	;
10444               	; 	' ======================================================================
10445               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10446               	; 	' ======================================================================
10447               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10448               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10449               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10450               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10451               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10452               	; 	'
10453               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10454               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10455               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10456               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10457               	; 	' broken.
10458               	; 	'
10459               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10460               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10461               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10462               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10463               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10464               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10465               	; 	'
10466               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10467               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10468               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10469               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10470               	; coll_obst:
10471               cvb_COLL_OBST

     E2A8 219C     
10792               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10793               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10794               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10795               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10796               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10797               	; 	' away from.
10798               	; 	'
10799               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10800               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10801               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10802               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10803               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10804               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10805               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10806               	; 	'
10807               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10808               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10809               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10810               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10811               	; 	'
10812               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10813               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10814               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10815               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10816               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10817               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10818               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10819               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10820               	; 	'
10821               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10822               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.

10981               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
10982               	; 	'
10983               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
10984               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10985               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10986               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10987               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10988               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10989               	; 	'
10990               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10991               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10992               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
10993               	; 	'
10994               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
10995               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
10996               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
10997               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10998               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
10999               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
11000               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

11106               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.

11110               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11111               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11112               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11113               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11114               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11115               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.

11354               	; 		' divide -- `/` compiles to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and
11355               	; 		' this is per-frame code. Two adjacent bits give 0,4,8,12.

11357               	; 		' KELLY USES BITS 2 AND 3 AND HARRY USES 3 AND 4, because a stride
11358               	; 		' has to cover about a stride's worth of ground or the figure
11359               	; 		' skates. Kelly runs 4 px a frame, so four frames a pose is 16 px;
11360               	; 		' Harry runs 1.75, so eight frames a pose is 14. Matching the two

12237               	;
12238               	; 	' ======================================================================
12239               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12240               	; 	' ======================================================================
12241               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12242               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12243               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12244               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12245               	; 	'
12246               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12247               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12248               	; 	'
12249               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12250               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12251               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12252               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12253               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12254               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12255               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12256               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12257               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12258               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12259               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12260               	; esc_tick:
12261               cvb_ESC_TICK
12262               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
12263               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12264               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12265               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12266               	; 	IF klsc > 0 THEN
12267 ED78 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     ED7A 21AC     
12268 ED7C 0201  20 	li r1,256   ; 1*256
     ED7E 0100

12270 ED82 1402  14 	jhe cv835
12271 ED84 0460  28 	b @cv834
     ED86 ED9C     
12272               cv835

12274 ED88 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     ED8A 21AC

     ED8E 0700

12284               cv834
12285               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12286               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12287               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12288               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12289               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12290               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12291               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12292               	; 	'
12293               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --

12596               	;
12597               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12598               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12599               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12600               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12601               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12602               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12603               	; 	'
12604               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12605               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12606               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12607               	; 	'
12608               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12609               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12610               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12611               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12612               	; 	'
12613               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12614               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12615               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12616               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12617               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12618               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12619               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12620               	; 	'
12621               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12622               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12623               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12624               	; 	'
12625               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12626               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12627               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.

12971               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12972               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12973               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12974               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12975               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12976               	; scan_wipe:

12978               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12979               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12980               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12981               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12982               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12983               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12984               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12985               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12986               	; 	'
12987               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12988               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12989               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12990               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12991               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12992               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12993               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12994               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12995               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12996               	; 	'
12997               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12998               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12999               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
13000               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
13001               	; 	'
13002               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
13003               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

13073               	; 	' THE TWO ACTORS ARE SPRITES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS CHARACTERS.
13074               	; 	'
13075               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
13076               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
13077               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
13078               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
13079               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the
13080               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
13081               	; 	'
13082               	; 	' IT ALSO REMOVED THE BLINK. Kelly flashed because a pixel row of this
13083               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers
13084               	; 	' merged and the blink was the only thing left to tell them apart. Two
13085               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.
13086               	; 	'
13087               	; 	' The furniture is drawn ONCE, by scan_furn. It used to be redrawn every
13088               	; 	' tick because erasing a character-based marker ANDed bits out of
13089               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
13090               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.
13091               	; 	' -- the lift car. IT WAS FLICKERING, and the cause was not the drawing
13092               	; 	' but the ERASING: scan_elev cleared its three cells and put them back
13093               	; 	' every tick, whether or not the car had moved, so several times a second
13094               	; 	' there was a window with the pixels off. A sprite has no erase at all --
13095               	; 	' it is placed, and the VDP does the rest -- and slot 26 sits BELOW the

13881               	;
13882               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13883               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13884               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13885               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13886               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13887               	; 	'
13888               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13889               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13890               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13891               	; 	'
13892               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13893               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13894               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13895               	; 	'
13896               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13897               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13898               	; 	'
13899               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13900               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13901               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13902               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13903               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13904               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13905               	; 	'
13906               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13907               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13908               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13909               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13910               	; 	'
13911               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13912               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13913               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13914               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
13915               	; bonus_count:

14031               	;
14032               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14033               	; 	'
14034               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14035               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14036               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14037               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14038               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14039               	; 	'
14040               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14041               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14042               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14043               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14044               	; 	' counting stops.
14045               	;
14046               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14047               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14048               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14049               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14050               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14051               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14052               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14053               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14054               	; 	'
14055               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14056               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14057               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

14105               	; 	' THE MESSAGE BOX, ON THE GAME SCREEN AND NOT INSTEAD OF IT.
14106               	; 	'
14107               	; 	' It used to CLS before GAME OVER, so the last thing the player saw was
14108               	; 	' the store being deleted and then two words on an empty field -- which
14109               	; 	' reads as the program ending rather than as the game ending. The store
14110               	; 	' stays; the message sits in the middle of it.
14111               	; 	'
14112               	; 	' THE BOX IS THE FONT'S OWN BACKGROUND. Every font character is black on
14113               	; 	' HUD_BG (dark blue), so a row of SPACES is a solid dark blue bar. A blank
14114               	; 	' row above and below the text is a frame for the price of two strings and
14115               	; 	' no new characters, and it reads against the store because nothing else on
14116               	; 	' the playfield is that colour.
14117               	; 	'
14118               	; 	' THIRTEEN WIDE, WHICH IS THE LONGEST MESSAGE PLUS ONE EITHER SIDE.
14119               	; 	' HE GOT AWAY and THE BIPLANE are both eleven. Every string below is padded

14660               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14661               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14662               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14663               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14664               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14665               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14666               	;
14667               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14668               	; 	'
14669               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14670               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14671               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14672               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14673               	; 	'
14674               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14675               	; 	'
14676               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14677               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14678               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14679               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14680               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14681               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14682               	; 	'
14683               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14684               	; 	'
14685               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14686               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14687               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14688               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14689               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14690               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14691               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14692               	; 	'
14693               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14694               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14695               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14696               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14697               	; 	'
14698               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14699               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14700               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14701               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14702               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14703               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14704               	; 	'
14705               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14706               	; 	'
14707               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize

14836 FEF2 0450  20 	b *r0
14837               	;
14838               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14839               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14840               	; 	'
14841               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14842               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14843               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14844               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14845               	; 	'
14846               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14847               	; 	'
14848               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14849               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14850               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14851               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14852               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14853               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14854               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14855               	; 	'
14856               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14857               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14858               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14859               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14860               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14861               	; 	'
14862               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14863               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14864               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14865               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14866               	; 	#if TI994A
14867               	; 	BANK 2
14868      010A     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

15532               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15533               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15534               	; 	'
15535               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15536               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15537               	; 	' being small sprites.
15538               	; 	'
15539               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15540               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15541               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15542               	; 	'
15543               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15544               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15545               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15546               	;
15547               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15548               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16678               	; 	' -------------------------------------------------- scanner canvas
16679               	; 	' Chars 208-255: 16 cols x 3 rows over screen rows 21-23. Blank to start;
16680               	; 	' dots are plotted by VPOKEing the PATTERN table (rows 21-23 sit in the
16681               	; 	' third screen third, so every scanner pattern is at base 4096).
16682               	;
16683               	; 	' --------------------------------------------------- font colours
16684               	; 	' Chars 32-90, EIGHT bytes each. Without this the font keeps whatever
16685               	; 	' CVBasic left in the colour table, which on a green store made the HUD
16686               	; 	' unreadable.
16687               	;
16688               	; scan_col3:	' one 8-byte block per canvas row: 4 px of GREY margin, then a 3 px band of furniture GREY and a yellow floor line, per 4 px level, on dark green. The Kop and the crook are coloured PER CHARACTER at run time -- see scan_set
16689               cvb_SCAN_COL3

16804               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16805               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16806               	; 	'
16807               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16808               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16809               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16810               	; 	'
16811               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16812               	; 	' blit is
16813               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16814               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16815               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16816               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16817               	; 	'
16818               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16819               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16820               	; 	'
16821               	; 	' template ids:
16822               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16823               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16824               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16825               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16826               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16827               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16828               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16829               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16830               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16831               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16832               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16833               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16834               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16835               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16836               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
